partners.mechanism_chain: PLG (HGNC:9420) —DISRUPTS→ Fibrinolysis (P00054); Fibrinolysis (P00054) —DECREASES→ Bradykinin (CHEBI:17614); Bradykinin (CHEBI:17614) —INCREASES→ Angioedema (HP:0000252); HTRA1 (HGNC:24765) —DISRUPTS→ TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP490); TGF-beta signaling pathway (WP490) —LEADS_TO→ Cerebral small vessel disease (HP:0030141). Loss-of-function mutations in PLG (encoding plasminogen) impair fibrinolysis, leading to increased bradykinin levels and angioedema. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in HTRA1 impair the degradation of TGF-beta, contributing to cerebral small vessel disease seen in CARASIL. The convergence lies in the dysregulation of distinct but interconnected extracellular matrix remodeling and signaling pathways, highlighting a shared vulnerability in vascular integrity, albeit through different molecular mediators. While PLG directly impacts fibrinolysis and bradykinin, HTRA1's role in TGF-beta degradation affects extracellular matrix deposition and vascular health. The shared mechanism is the dysregulation of pathways critical for vascular homeostasis.
